title: Per-token IO split probe: streaming floor smoothing + enterprise QA alignment
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Customers and sales have repeatedly asked for clearer economics when applications use asymmetric I/O patterns (short prompts, long generations) and streaming responses. Our current per-token billing conflates ingress/egress which creates mismatch for streaming-first products and for enterprise contracts that require predictable minima.

Objective: Run a 6-week field probe to evaluate a split per-token meter (ingress vs egress) with a streaming-specific minimum (stream-floor) that smooths spikes for low-volume streaming customers. Evaluate revenue delta, churn signal, and sales enablement effort required to reflect this model in contracts and security questionnaires.

Hypotheses:
- H1: Introducing an explicit ingress/egress split with a modest streaming floor will reduce perceived overbilling for streaming-first customers and increase trial-to-paid conversion for real-time apps by at least 8% in targeted cohorts.
- H2: Net revenue per active customer will be neutral to positive after adjusting floor levels; some high-egress customers may shift to reserved/dedicated offers.
- H3: Enterprise contract and security questionnaire changes (clarified metering + examples) will shorten procurement cycles by 10% for mid-market deals.

Success metrics:
- Conversion rate change: +8% for streaming-focused signups in experiment cohort.
- ARPA delta: within -5% to +10% vs control.
- Support/Manual Billing asks: <= 20% increase in billing disputes per cohort.
- Sales procurement lead time: -10% for deals where we surface the new meter in SOW/QA.
- Technical impact: <3% increase in API request latency at ingress point due to new metering tagging.
experimental_design:
Cohort selection: Identify two cohorts of new signups and existing small customers (n≈600 total) with streaming-heavy usage and comparable baseline spend. Randomized A/B: control = current unified per-token meter; variant = split-meter (ingress tokens charged at rate A, egress tokens charged at rate B) + streaming floor credit that applies when streaming egress > X tokens but monthly spend < floor threshold.

Pricing parameters to test (matrix):
- ingress_rate: $0.0008/token, egress_rate: $0.0016/token, stream_floor: $7/month
- ingress_rate: $0.0009/token, egress_rate: $0.0014/token, stream_floor: $10/month
- ingress_rate: $0.0007/token, egress_rate: $0.0018/token, stream_floor: $5/month

Measurement window: 30 days active usage per cohort, with 30-day revenue follow-up. Billing integration: Variant applies retroactively to the cohort for the test months and is visible in billing UI. Accounting will run side-by-side simulation to ensure no invoicing issues.
rollout_plan: 1) Week 0: Instrument metering tags (ingress/egress) and streaming handshake detection; feature flag the split-meter calculation. 2) Week 1: Internal smoke test on sandbox customers and finance reconciliation. 3) Week 2-5: Run experiment cohorts; daily dashboards and weekly executive summaries. 4) Week 6: Evaluate, pick winning parameters; prepare PRD to extend to a broader beta. 5) Post-experiment: update billing docs, sales one-pager, and enterprise contract templates with example billing scenarios.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Confusion for existing customers leading to billing disputes. Mitigation: We surface a clear comparison in the console showing "previous bill vs new-meter simulation" and provide an opt-in month where customers can preview the new breakdown.

Risk: Accountants/Finance reconciliation complexity. Mitigation: Keep variant as a simulation for accounting (no actual invoices changed) for the first cohort; finance-run reconciliation and a short operational playbook.

Risk: Legal/enterprise QA pushback on meter semantics. Mitigation: Engage Legal and Trust early; draft standard secure wording for security questionnaires that explains metering and data handling; create a short appendix for SOWs that itemizes the meter definitions.
